name: Grunge
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference: worn paper and rough substrates with distressed ink, scratches, stains, local erasures and incomplete lettering. Keep texture scale and density controlled so the main message remains clear; avoid persistent noise or darkening the full frame.
suitableUses: Explicitly suggested for texture-led title sequences and mood pieces. Compatible examples include music promos, documentary chapter titles, gritty brand statements, atmospheric intros and album visualizers. It may also support explanatory or cinematic narratives when the worn surface stays primary. Suitability for these broader uses is inferred, not a canonical source claim.
limitations: The source does not claim this as a directly named style in its collection. Avoid obscuring text or subjects with noise, transitions that impair communication, and unsupported chapter changes. Glitch is only suitable for intentionally abrasive transitions; omit it for calm editorial scenes. No fixed duration, aspect ratio or required scene count is specified.
palette: For new artwork without an approved palette, suggested tokens are background worn paper #E4DCCD, foreground charcoal #302E29, and subordinate oxidized-red accent #8C5140. These are authored suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve exact task, brand, reference and asset colors and their roles; do not recolor subjects, expand hues, or add gradients. Check contrast on actual composites; the suggested charcoal/paper pair is 9.957:1 and accent/paper is 4.58:1, but neither guarantees readability over texture or imagery.
motionAndInteraction: Precompute distressed masks, ink textures and paper grain; reveal them locally and reuse them deterministically. Keep settled lettering readable, with holds. Optional typography sequencing reveals one word at a time; restrained parallax may separate substrate layers. For interactive HTML, scroll may control chapters or story states, with backward movement restoring matching states and reduced-motion fallbacks. Glitch cuts, if justified, use a narrow bounded transition and clean endpoints. Video must use seekable composition time, never live scroll input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is prescribed. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience, honoring supplied audio choices. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping and competing vocals, synchronize audio with picture, and inspect them together.
assetRequirements: Prepare and cache distressed masks, ink textures and paper grain; use the same textures each render. Load fonts and assets locally, seed randomness, and make visual state deterministic. Rough.js is optional for seeded sketch-like contours or hachure only; it does not provide handwriting, authentic print media, brush simulation, paper texture or animation. Preserve approved source artwork.
combinations: Works alone for texture-led titles and mood pieces. Optional paced typography (style-093) can reveal distressed words in sequence; optional substrate parallax (style-101) adds restrained depth. Both combinations specify the three-token palette, reused masks and readable settled text. Do not cover text with noise, darken the whole frame, use bouncy easing, expose parallax edges or add glossy blur. Other combinations are unspecified.
productionApproach: Choose visual and motion methods for the style and action first. Canvas 2D is the suggested renderer; Python/Pillow can preprocess textures. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation and export pipeline; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, with reason recorded. GSAP supplies a paused seekable timeline. Keep rendering, motion and export responsibilities separate; inspect representative frames and the full video.
